question: Does translation-invariant polyphase max pooling keep a classifier's accuracy more stable under small input shifts than standard stride-2 max pooling on the digits dataset?
method: Same pooled-feature standardized logistic regression (C tuned by 5-fold CV on training data) trained on unshifted train images; test accuracy averaged over 25 circular shifts (up to 2 px).

dataset.name: Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits (scikit-learn load_digits)

metric_name: mean test accuracy over 25 circular shifts (up to 2 px in each direction)
baseline: Standard 2x2 max pooling with stride 2 (8x8 -> 4x4) followed by standardized logistic regression.
improved: Dense stride-1 2x2 max pooling whose four stride-2 polyphase sub-grids are combined by elementwise maximum (8x8 -> 4x4), followed by the same classifier.
notes: Single deterministic run: logistic regression is deterministic, so seeds 42-44 were not needed; the score_std values are the spread across the 25 shifts, not across seeds. The baseline is a stand-in for CNN pooling; the paper's exact polyphase selection rule was not re-implemented. Elementwise max over the four phases effectively enlarges the pooling window to about 3x3, so any gain may reflect a larger receptive field rather than polyphase sampling per se. Only 8x8 images with a linear classifier were used, so results may not transfer to deep CNNs. Test set used once for final scores; no selection on it.
